answer: Every claim must pass the summit tool check. Before filing, the filer brings the tools the work was done with to the summit hut, where the kernel clerk wipes each one with walnut oil and logs the wear in the kernel book within a day: a saw that cut forty planks must show forty planks of wear, and oil that stays pale on a supposedly used blade means rejection and a lost 250-coin bond, so 1,000 fakes need 1,000 genuinely worn tool sets plus 250,000 coins. One operator filed forty claims with tools straight from the shop shelf, and all forty failed when the oil stayed pale on every blade.
